correctness.rationale: For f indexed from 1, f(2t)=f(t) and odd-index bits alternate. No four-letter factor of f alternates. Every factor of even length at least eight has exactly one alternating parity track, so its occurrence start parity is intrinsic. If n is divisible by four, rotation by r shifts that parity by r modulo two. Interleaving an n-factor w beginning at t with f(2(t+j)+1) gives an actual 2n-factor; every 2n-factor is conjugate to such a lift, including those starting at odd positions. The lift respects source conjugacy. Conversely, uniqueness of the alternating track forces any conjugating shift of two lifts to be even, and the decimated source factors must be conjugate. Thus the orbit map is a bijection, including all n>=8 divisible by four; n=4 is a verified exception. The independently executable verifier checks both digit definitions, completeness of tested finite factor sets, and 20 exact doubling pairs.

value.rationale: The 2014 cyclic-complexity theorem isolates a single power-of-two ray. The new structural parity-track bijection makes cyclic factor complexity exactly invariant under doubling on all multiples of four from eight onward, yields distinct infinite families with c(12*2^j)=16, c(20*2^j)=28, c(28*2^j)=40, and identifies the sharp obstruction at n=4. This is a motivated infinite structural classification, not a routine numerical increment or factor-count restatement.
